rappel_detail.pull: A single 60 m rope reaches the ledge with room to spare. Knot both ends as a matter of habit.
rappel_detail.notes: Reached by downclimbing the upper pitch about 20 ft from the summit, then moving left (east). First of the three single-rope rappels.
hazards: These trees are the only marker for the top of the descent and are easy to walk past on the summit ridge; a party that misses them commits itself to downclimbing the loose east gully instead.
The lower tree's slings are periodically found tired. Carry cord or webbing to replace rather than rappelling on whatever happens to be there.
Snow can linger on the landing ledge into early season.
rappel_detail.station: Reverse the last pitch roughly 15-20 m (about 50 ft) from the summit and work toward the Concord Tower side of the crest. The anchor is a tree carrying fixed slings, tucked off the crest near a shallow groove in the rock; two slung trees stand close together and the upper one is the sounder of the pair. It is much easier to pick out while leading pitch 4 than from above, so note it on the way up. The rappel lands on a sandy, tree-dotted ledge.

rappel_detail.pull: A plumb pull off bolts. Keep the strands clear of the ledge lip and its trees so nothing catches on the retrieve.
rappel_detail.notes: Second station, on a large ledge reached by scrambling down and to the right from the first rappel.
hazards: Loose sand and grit on the ledge above slabby downclimbing.
If the chains are not found after the ropes are pulled, the party is stranded between stations with no anchor.
rappel_detail.station: Do not rappel straight on from the sandy ledge. Work right along the ledge, then down, then right again to reach a fixed station of bolts and chains on the steep wall. Parties consistently report this hardware as hard to spot, so scout it before pulling the first rope.

rappel_detail.pull: Because the rappel is diagonal, the pull strand drags across the wall and this descent has a documented history of jammed ropes. One party had to fix one strand, lead back up the climbable ground to free it, then ascend to the station and re-rig. Feed the pull strand out and away from the diagonal, and pull from the notch rather than from directly under the anchor.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappels somewhat diagonally into the Liberty Bell-Concord notch at about 7,300 ft. Downclimb the gully from there to the packs.
hazards: The line traverses, so anyone who loses the stance swings across the wall.
The notch and the gully below it are loose, and anything dislodged here funnels onto the climbers' path that other parties are walking up.
rappel_detail.station: The lowest fixed station on the wall, straight below the previous one. The rappel from it runs slightly diagonally rather than plumb and finishes in the Liberty Bell-Concord notch at roughly 7,300 ft, close to where most parties leave packs at the top of the approach gully.

set.rappels: 3 single-rope rappels with a 60 m rope on the standard Liberty Bell descent: one off slung trees just below the summit, then two of about 25 m from bolted anchors into the Liberty Bell-Concord notch. Downclimbing the first section instead leaves two.
set.rappel_count_note: This route finishes on Liberty Bell and takes the standard descent. Three rappels on a single 60 m rope, which is the rope this route recommends and the configuration these three stations describe. The count of two comes from the same station set rather than a different one: the first rappel, off the trees, is optional and replaces a downclimb of the ridge and the 5.6 boulder problem, so a party that downclimbs that section starts at the second station and reaches the ground in two single-rope rappels. Accounts recording two and accounts recording three are describing the same anchors. The two lower rappels are reported at about 25 m each, and a single 60 m rope reaches the first ledge with room to spare. This is the standard descent line shared with the East Face and Northwest Face routes.
set.descent_text: Serpentine Crack finishes on an exposed, sunny arete with a 5.7 simul-climb or scramble to the true summit, so the descent is the standard one used by all summit-topping Liberty Bell lines. From the summit, downclimb the upper pitch a short way and go left (east) to a tree hung with rappel slings. One single-rope rappel with a 60 m rope reaches a sandy ledge; work right and down to a bolted station, then make two single-rope rappels of about 25 m from bolted anchors into the Liberty Bell-Concord notch at about 7,300 ft. Parties who downclimb the ridge and the 5.6 boulder problem to the first bolts instead of making the tree rappel do two rappels in all. From the notch, downclimb the loose gully back to the climbers’ path and the Blue Lake Trail.
set.descent: From the summit, downclimb (or rappel) the upper pitch a short way, then go left (east) to a slung tree for a single-rope rappel to a ledge. From the bolted station below, one double-rope rappel or two single-rope rappels (a 60m rope is recommended) reach the Liberty Bell-Concord notch at ~7,300 ft, from which parties descend the approach gully back to the climbers' path.
